content.summary: The literal statement, ordinary computer-assisted assurance level, arbitrary-support scope, and claimed contribution are coherently framed. The size-68 hereditary reduction and elementary graph transfers are sound, and the inspected new-lemma support reduction has the right whole-completion quantifiers. No contract-framing defect requiring a manuscript change was found. Continue to detailed proof and finite-evidence review; this round does not certify every active finite exclusion or the imported computational theorems.

findings.statement: The intended improvement is an ordinary maximum-size bound M(4,3)<=67, equivalently a forcing threshold of 68, for simple exactly four-uniform families including empty-core sunflowers.
findings.disposition: Manuscript sections 1 and 3 and GLOBAL67-ordinary-theorem.md, Literal statement, agree on these conventions. No convention repair is needed.

findings.statement: The new fifteen-triple result is stated on arbitrary support, while its final finite trees run on eleven labels; the support-reduction bridge is therefore an essential part of the contribution.
findings.disposition: The linked ordinary check explicitly bounds new points across the entire six-triple completion and derives support at most eleven only after eliminating degrees one and two. The framing preserves this obligation. I inspected this reasoning and checked its scalar bounds, but did not replay the motif exclusions or final trees in this round.

findings.statement: Imported H27, Jin and prior structural packages are distinguished from new local proofs and from Lean assurance.
findings.disposition: Manuscript sections 2, 3 and 7 and the external-scope note disclose the unreplayed H27 ledger, Jin's scholarly restatement, selected prior replays and shared model builders. These are appropriate claim boundaries; my present inspection does not independently establish the external theorem proofs or exhaustive priority.

checks.scope: Frozen round-one identities and selected evidence integrity
checks.method: Read the protocol, manuscript, contract, roster and snapshot; compute SHA256 of manuscript bytes and canonical sorted compact JSON; hash the five inspected snapshot evidence entries.
checks.observation: The manuscript hash is 2c200bf5dff9e665e7dab3ba3f5a1ef019251d341a1913d1f5bd2fc3c086f937 and canonical snapshot hash is 7912a1f1de1f27d72b2a2e660626f338303bf8cf71085720b4c1e304e670b5ba. All five selected evidence hashes match. The roster role and context are beta and /root/r67_beta.

checks.scope: Literal quantifiers, hereditary reduction and neighbourhood foundation
checks.method: Independently follow the set-theoretic implications in manuscript sections 1 and 3, GLOBAL67-ordinary-theorem.md, Mathematical proof by maximum degree, and roadmap section 1.
checks.observation: Restricting to any 68 members preserves simplicity, exact uniformity and sunflower-freeness. For an actual R, two disjoint members of its disjoint class would form an empty-core sunflower with R, so H27 applies to that class and gives |N[R]|>=41. Independent sets of the disjointness graph are intersecting SF4 subfamilies. The fixed-subfamily convention avoids inheriting minimum positive degree through deletion.

checks.scope: Degree-case coverage and placement of guarded imports
checks.method: Inspect GLOBAL67-dependency-roadmap.md sections 1 and 2 and compare with manuscript sections 4 through 6.
checks.observation: The displayed chain exhausts Delta=20,19,18,17,16 and Delta<=15. The cap18/mu41 package is introduced only after the degree19 exclusion; the roadmap expressly excludes use of the old size69 conclusion as a size68 premise. This verifies the stated dependency architecture, not every underlying branch proof.

checks.scope: Arbitrary-support meaning of the new fifteen-triple contribution
checks.method: Read R15-rho6-completed-evidence.md and its named R15-degree2-independent-ordinary-check.md, especially Whole-completion exterior bound and Eleven-point support and complete root cases; check the displayed rational inequalities with Python standard-library Fraction arithmetic.
checks.observation: The bridge bounds the number of new-point triples by the sum of remaining old-pair capacities, at most three, thereby also bounding total new points. For degrees 3,4,5,6, the displayed summands 5/2,5,8,12 are at most 19d/6-7. The exact checks give 285/2-7*12<60 and 225/4<60, supporting n<=11 and existence of a degree5 or6 point once the preceding low-degree exclusions hold.

checks.scope: Direct Jin A3 interface and absence of an assumed surjectivity premise
checks.method: Read LOW15-direct-Jin-A3-addon.md; independently expand the cyclic coefficient identity for all eight indices using a bounded standard-library script.
checks.observation: For every i, b_i+b_(i+3)+b_(i+5) counts each fibre once and fibre i twice. The strict threshold has integer margin 25*11-4*68=3. The derivation first uses b_i<=27 for all indices, obtains a_i>=1 from total deficit 12, and only then uses b_i>=25. No complete-blowup or initially surjective-map assumption is introduced.

checks.method: Compare manuscript abstract, sections 2 and 7, and conclusion with GLOBAL67-ordinary-theorem.md and EXTERNAL-H27-JIN-SCOPE.md.
checks.observation: The contribution is confined to the located rank-four upper bound and specified new structural/computational components. The text expressly excludes an all-rank theorem, exhaustive global originality, end-to-end Lean verification, full local H27 replay and independent human certification. I did not independently repeat the literature search or external ledger in this round.
